problem: Suppose that $f(x)$ is a function such that ${\int }_{3}^{0}\frac{1}{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-1$ and ${\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=6.$ What is the value of ${\int }_{0}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x?$
worked_solution:
Let's simplify one of the given integrals:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{0}\frac{1}{3}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-1 \\ \frac{1}{3}{\int }_{3}^{0}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-1 \\ -\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-1 \\ {\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Then, from the adjacent intervals rule, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3+6 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$
